newsitem.title: UK: TI falls despite planned earnings upgrades.
newsitem.headline: TI falls despite planned earnings upgrades.

text.p: Shares in engineering group TI opened lower on Thursday despite results at the top of analysts expectations and planned upward revisions to earnings forecasts.
The shares were down 19p at 550p by 0740 GMT on profit-taking after gains of 55p in the last two days on the back of a weaker pound which was seen helping currency translation.
"The shares have bounced very sharply with the falling pound after being hit hard by the currency," said Tim Bennett, engineering analyst at Morgan Stanley. "It's probably just some profit-taking."
Bennett said he would probably make a slight upwards revision to his earnings forecast for the group on the back of a better than expected performance by the company's aerospace business.
TI reported pretax profits of 112 million stg, above average forecasts around 110 million stg and up eight percent from 103.7 million stg pre-exceptional profit the previous year.
"The results were in line with expectations," said Bennett, but the mix was different to our expectations."
"Aerospace was even better than expected whilst Crane, the seals division was disappointing," the analyst said.
John Crane Group achieved organic sales growth of two percent in challenging market conditions whilst Dowty enjoyed sales growth of 23 percent.
The effect of the strengthening of sterling on the translation of overseas profits reduced the pretax figure by 7.6 million stg, broadly in line with expectations, Bennett said.
